walkthroughs.h2: The Cratchits as the working poor
walkthroughs.body_html:
Bob earns just 15 shillings a week — barely enough to feed his family.

Dickens shows them celebrating Christmas joyfully despite poverty. This shames Scrooge, whose wealth has not bought him happiness.

walkthroughs.h2: Tiny Tim as a moral test
walkthroughs.body_html:
Tiny Tim is disabled and the family cannot afford the care he needs.

The Ghost of Christmas Present warns 'If these shadows remain unaltered… the child will die.' Dickens uses Tim to attack the indifference of Malthusian thinkers.

In Stave 3 the Ghost reveals two starving children clinging to his robes.

They are an allegory: Ignorance (lack of education) and Want (poverty). The Ghost warns 'Most of all beware this boy' — Ignorance, the deeper threat.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between a theme and a symbol?
options: Epic means any story with a battle in it.
Themes are just symbols repeated through the book.
A theme is an abstract idea or concern the text explores (e.g. mortality); a symbol is a concrete image that stands for something else (e.g. a skull).
A theme is the title of the book.
Epic means any story with a battle in it.
Modernism is literature about modern technology like phones.
Modernism just means literature written in modern times.
Experimentation with form (fragmentation, stream of consciousness), focus on subjective interior experience, scepticism toward traditional narrative and absolute truth.
